*GETTING READY TABLE 1*

*FREQUENCIES AND PERCENTAGES BY GENDER*

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

variables <- c( # List of variables
  "Age_Group",
  "Education_Level_Final",
  "Ethnicity",
  "Country",
  "Neuroticism_Level",
  "Extraversion_Level",
  "Openness_Level",
  "Agreeableness_Level",
  "Conscientiousness_Level",
  "Impulsivity_Level",
  "Sensation_Seeking_Level",
  "Caffeine_Use", 
  "Nicotine_Use", 
  "Alcohol_Use",
  "Chocolate_Use",
  "Cocaine_Use", 
  "Ketamine_Use", 
  "Heroin_Use", 
  "LSD_Use"
)

format_label <- function(var_name) {
  text <- gsub("_", " ", var_name)
  text <- tolower(text)
  text <- tools::toTitleCase(text)
  return(text)
}

for (var in variables) {
  if (!(var %in% names(data_drugs))) {
    message(paste("Column", var, "not found in data_drugs. Skipping."))
    next
  }
  
  var_label <- format_label(var)
  
  df_var <- data_drugs %>%   # Keep only Gender and the variable of interest
    select(Gender, value = all_of(var)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(Gender))
  
  total_tab <- df_var %>%   # Overall totals
    group_by(value) %>%
    summarize(
      Total_n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Total_pct = round(Total_n / sum(Total_n) * 100, 1)
    )
  
  gender_tab <- df_var %>%   # Totals by gender
    group_by(Gender, value) %>%
    summarize(
      n = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(Gender) %>%
    mutate(
      pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = Gender,
      values_from = c(n, pct),
      names_sep = "_"
    )
  
  final_table <- total_tab %>%   # Merge overall and by-gender information
    left_join(gender_tab, by = "value") %>%
    arrange(desc(Total_n))
  
  colnames(final_table) <- gsub("^n_Female$", "Female_n", colnames(final_table))
  colnames(final_table) <- gsub("^pct_Female$", "Female_pct", colnames(final_table))
  colnames(final_table) <- gsub("^n_Male$", "Male_n", colnames(final_table))
  colnames(final_table) <- gsub("^pct_Male$", "Male_pct", colnames(final_table))
  
  final_table <- final_table %>%
    mutate(
      Total_n  = as.integer(Total_n),
      Female_n = as.integer(Female_n),
      Male_n   = as.integer(Male_n)
    )
  
  final_table <- final_table %>%   # Reorder columns to match the labels

    select(
      value,
      Total_n,
      Total_pct,
      Female_n,
      Female_pct,
      Male_n,
      Male_pct
    )
  
  cat("\n\n**Variable:** ", var_label, "\n\n")
  
  print(
    kable(
      final_table,
      col.names = c(
        var_label,
        "Total n",
        "Total %",
        "Female n",
        "Female %",
        "Male n",
        "Male %"
      ),
      align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = paste("Frequency and percentage of", var_label, "by gender")
    )
  )
}



```

*GETTING P VALUES TABLE 1*
= USING CHI SQUARE, BECAUSE ALL THIS VARIABLES ARE NOMINAL CATEGORICAL, WITH MULTIPLE CATEGORIES. COMPARING BETWEEN GROUPS (MALE AND FEMALE)

```{r pvalues-table1, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
vars_table1 <- c(
  "Age_Group",
  "Education_Level_Final",
  "Ethnicity",
  "Country",
  "Neuroticism_Level",
  "Extraversion_Level",
  "Openness_Level",
  "Agreeableness_Level",
  "Conscientiousness_Level",
  "Impulsivity_Level",
  "Sensation_Seeking_Level",
  
  # Legal drug use (User vs Non-user)
  "Caffeine_Use",
  "Nicotine_Use",
  "Alcohol_Use",
  "Chocolate_Use",
  
  # Illegal drug use (User vs Non-user)
  "Cocaine_Use",
  "Ketamine_Use",
  "Heroin_Use",
  "LSD_Use"
)

# Function / p-value for association between a variable and Gender
compute_p <- function(var_name) {
  
  # Contingency table: rows = categories of var, columns = Gender
  tab <- table(data_drugs[[var_name]], data_drugs$Gender)
  
  # Try chi-square test first
  chi_try <- suppressWarnings(try(chisq.test(tab), silent = TRUE))
  
  # If chi-square completely fails, fall back
  if (inherits(chi_try, "try-error")) {
    if (nrow(tab) == 2 && ncol(tab) == 2) {
      # 2x2 table → Fisher's exact test
      test <- fisher.test(tab)
      return(round(test$p.value, 4))
    } else {
      # Larger table → chi-square 
      test <- chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
      return(round(test$p.value, 4))
    }
  }
  
  # If chi-square worked, inspect expected counts
  exp_counts <- chi_try$expected
  
  # Case 1: all expected counts >= 5 → standard chi-square
  if (all(exp_counts >= 5)) {
    pval <- chi_try$p.value
    
  # Case 2: small expected counts and 2x2 table → Fisher's exact test
  } else if (nrow(tab) == 2 && ncol(tab) == 2) {
    test <- fisher.test(tab)
    pval <- test$p.value
    
  # Case 3: small expected counts and larger table → chi-square with simulated p-value
  } else {
    test <- chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
    pval <- test$p.value
  }
  
  return(round(pval, 4))
}

# Compute p-values for all variables in Table 1
p_values_table1 <- data.frame(
  Variable = vars_table1,
  P_value  = sapply(vars_table1, compute_p)
)

p_values_table1
```

*GETTING READY TABLE 2*

```{r table2-frequencies, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#Create composite outcomes: Any legal / Any illegal drug use
data_drugs <- data_drugs %>%
  mutate(
    Any_Legal_Use = case_when(
      rowSums(across(
        c(Caffeine_Use, Nicotine_Use, Alcohol_Use, Chocolate_Use),
        ~ .x == "User"
      ), na.rm = TRUE) > 0 ~ "User",
      rowSums(across(
        c(Caffeine_Use, Nicotine_Use, Alcohol_Use, Chocolate_Use),
        ~ !is.na(.x)
      )) == 0 ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Non-user"
    ),
    Any_Illegal_Use = case_when(
      rowSums(across(
        c(Cocaine_Use, Ketamine_Use, Heroin_Use, LSD_Use),
        ~ .x == "User"
      ), na.rm = TRUE) > 0 ~ "User",
      rowSums(across(
        c(Cocaine_Use, Ketamine_Use, Heroin_Use, LSD_Use),
        ~ !is.na(.x)
      )) == 0 ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "Non-user"
    )
  )

#Table by Age group
table2_age <- data_drugs %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age_Group)) %>%
  group_by(Age_Group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Any_Legal_User_n   = sum(Any_Legal_Use == "User", na.rm = TRUE),
    Any_Legal_User_pct = round(Any_Legal_User_n / n * 100, 1),
    Any_Illegal_User_n   = sum(Any_Illegal_Use == "User", na.rm = TRUE),
    Any_Illegal_User_pct = round(Any_Illegal_User_n / n * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Age_Group)

kable(
  table2_age,
  col.names = c(
    "Age group",
    "n",
    "Any legal drug use n",
    "Any legal drug use (%)",
    "Any illegal drug use n",

  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Prevalence of any legal and illegal drug use by age group"
)
```

*GETTING P VALUES TABLE 2*

```{r table2-pvalues, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

compute_p_assoc <- function(predictor, outcome) {
  
  tab <- table(data_drugs[[predictor]], data_drugs[[outcome]])
  
  # Try chi-square first
  chi_try <- suppressWarnings(try(chisq.test(tab), silent = TRUE))
  
  # If chi-square completely fails, use chi-square
  if (inherits(chi_try, "try-error")) {
    test <- chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
    return(round(test$p.value, 4))
  }
  
  exp_counts <- chi_try$expected
  
  # All expected counts >= 5 → standard chi-square
  if (all(exp_counts >= 5)) {
    pval <- chi_try$p.value
    
  # Small expected counts and 2x2 table → Fisher
  } else if (nrow(tab) == 2 && ncol(tab) == 2) {
    pval <- fisher.test(tab)$p.value
    
  # Small expected counts and larger table → chi-square 
  } else {
    pval <- chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)$p.value
  }
  
  round(pval, 4)
}

# Define the four associations of interest
p_table2 <- data.frame(
  Predictor = c("Age_Group", "Age_Group",
                "Education_Level_Final", "Education_Level_Final"),
  Outcome   = c("Any_Legal_Use", "Any_Illegal_Use",
                "Any_Legal_Use", "Any_Illegal_Use")
) %>%
  mutate(
    P_value = mapply(compute_p_assoc, Predictor, Outcome),
    Predictor = dplyr::recode(Predictor,
                              "Age_Group" = "Age group",
                              "Education_Level_Final" = "Education level"),
    Outcome = dplyr::recode(Outcome,
                            "Any_Legal_Use"   = "Any legal drug use",
                            "Any_Illegal_Use" = "Any illegal drug use")
  )

# Show table with p-values
kable(
  p_table2,
  col.names = c("Characteristic", "Outcome", "P value"),
  align = c("l", "l", "r"),
  caption = "P values for the association between age, education and any legal/illegal drug use"
)

```


*TABLE 3*

```{r}
# Ensure outcome is a factor with "Non-user" 
data_drugs$Any_Illegal_Use_bin <- factor(
  ifelse(data_drugs$Any_Illegal_Use == "User", "User", "Non-user"),
  levels = c("Non-user", "User")
)

# Ensure Sensation Seeking Level has "Low" as reference
data_drugs$Sensation_Seeking_Level <- factor(
  data_drugs$Sensation_Seeking_Level,
  levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")
)

model_crude <- glm(
  Any_Illegal_Use_bin ~ Sensation_Seeking_Level,
  data = data_drugs,
  family = binomial
)

model_adj <- glm(
  Any_Illegal_Use_bin ~ Sensation_Seeking_Level + Gender + Age_Group + Education_Level_Final,
  data = data_drugs,
  family = binomial
)

extract_or <- function(model) {
  est <- coef(model)
  se  <- sqrt(diag(vcov(model)))
  or  <- exp(est)
  lower <- exp(est - 1.96 * se)
  upper <- exp(est + 1.96 * se)
  out <- data.frame(
    Term = names(est),
    OR = round(or, 2),
    CI_lower = round(lower, 2),
    CI_upper = round(upper, 2),
    row.names = NULL
  )
  out
}

or_crude <- extract_or(model_crude)
or_adj   <- extract_or(model_adj)

or_crude
or_adj


```

```{r logistic-any-illegal-all-traits, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Make sure outcome is binary factor 
data_drugs$Any_Illegal_Use_bin <- factor(
  ifelse(data_drugs$Any_Illegal_Use == "User", "User", "Non-user"),
  levels = c("Non-user", "User")
)

#Set references for covariates
data_drugs$Gender <- factor(data_drugs$Gender,
                            levels = c("Female", "Male"))

data_drugs$Age_Group <- factor(
  data_drugs$Age_Group,
  levels = c("18–24 years",
             "25–34 years",
             "35–44 years",
             "45–54 years",
             "55–64 years",
             "65+ years")
)

data_drugs$Education_Level_Final <- factor(
  data_drugs$Education_Level_Final,
  levels = c("High education", "Medium education", "Low education")
)

#Vector of personality level variables
trait_vars <- c(
  "Neuroticism_Level",
  "Extraversion_Level",
  "Openness_Level",
  "Agreeableness_Level",
  "Conscientiousness_Level",
  "Impulsivity_Level",
  "Sensation_Seeking_Level"
)

# Helper function to fit model and extract adjusted ORs for one trait
fit_trait_model <- function(trait_var) {
  
  # Ensure trait levels are ordered: Low (ref), Medium, High
  data_drugs[[trait_var]] <- factor(
    data_drugs[[trait_var]],
    levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High")
  )
  
  form <- as.formula(
    paste("Any_Illegal_Use_bin ~", trait_var,
          "+ Gender + Age_Group + Education_Level_Final")
  )
  
  model <- glm(form, data = data_drugs, family = binomial)
  
  # Extract coefficients and compute OR and 95% CI
  est <- coef(model)
  se  <- sqrt(diag(vcov(model)))
  or  <- exp(est)
  lower <- exp(est - 1.96 * se)
  upper <- exp(est + 1.96 * se)
  
  df <- data.frame(
    Term = names(est),
    OR = or,
    CI_lower = lower,
    CI_upper = upper,
    row.names = NULL
  )
  
  # Keep only Medium and High levels of the trait
  df_trait <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl(trait_var, Term)) %>%
    mutate(
      Trait = trait_var,
      Level = ifelse(grepl("Medium", Term), "Medium", "High")
    ) %>%
    select(Trait, Level, OR, CI_lower, CI_upper)
  
  df_trait
}

# Apply to all traits and bind rows
results_traits <- trait_vars %>%
  lapply(fit_trait_model) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  # Round for presentation
  mutate(
    OR = round(OR, 2),
    CI_lower = round(CI_lower, 2),
    CI_upper = round(CI_upper, 2),
    Trait = dplyr::recode(Trait,
      "Neuroticism_Level" = "Neuroticism",
      "Extraversion_Level" = "Extraversion",
      "Openness_Level" = "Openness",
      "Agreeableness_Level" = "Agreeableness",
      "Conscientiousness_Level" = "Conscientiousness",
      "Impulsivity_Level" = "Impulsivity",
      "Sensation_Seeking_Level" = "Sensation seeking"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Trait, Level)

results_traits
```
